dataFlow.produces: only the newly appended part is rasterized
live preview drawn from the WHOLE buffer (no region)

invariants.rule: Coverage is full inside the buffer; the stroke's opacity is applied exactly once, when the buffer composites. Overlapping segments must never darken the stroke.
Live preview, layer commit, undo/redo rebuild, reopen and PNG export produce the same pixels at every zoom and rasterScale.
A stroke is self-describing: it carries the brush it was drawn with; re-rasterizing never consults editor or tool state.
A stroke is exactly one undo step; StrokeCommand carries no pixels.
The vector samples stay authoritative; stamps are a rasterization strategy, not a new element kind.
Determinism: no Math.random(), no time, no zoom dependence in a repaint path.
The cost follows the inked area, not the document size; the rebuild clears and blends only the rectangle an element inks.
The brush is editor state: a brush change is not an edit.
DrawingRenderer and StrokeRecord remain the boundary.
Raster budget: at most 16,777,216 document px; peak 58 bytes per document pixel; the erase snapshot and the grouped-preview scratch are mutually exclusive.

stateOwnership.lifetime: per renderer; keyed by strength quantized to 1/20
only while a grouped preview is on screen

couplings.title: The bounded blit silently drops out-of-region coverage
couplings.detail: compositeStrokeBuffer composites only strokeRegion(stroke) (Canvas2DRenderer.ts:970,978), and strokeRegion is derived from strokeSampleBounds (935-949, 908-927) as samples +/- (strokeDiameter(brush,1)/2 + featherRadius*3 + 1). The live preview path draws the WHOLE buffer (paintDocument:670 -> paintStrokeCoverage without a region -> Canvas2DRenderer.ts:1028). Any coverage outside the bounds is visible while drawing and absent after the release.
couplings.impact: live vs commit divergence; silent loss of dab coverage for bristle, elongated, offset or wide-footprint stamps

couplings.title: rasterizeStroke's incremental contract is stateless; dab placement is not
couplings.detail: rasterizeStroke(ctx, stroke, fromIndex) reproduces the tail of a segment path from fromIndex alone. A dab's position depends on the previous dab's position, so the dab at the join between the drawn part and the appended part is not derivable from fromIndex.
couplings.impact: the incremental live path and the full rebuild path would place different dabs unless a cursor is introduced or dab placement is redefined as a pure function of the whole path

couplings.title: Canvas 2D has no max-alpha composite, so 'max/union' coverage is not directly available
couplings.detail: ROADMAP.md:212-214 requires per-dab coverage to be accumulated by max/union rather than repeated source-over, because source-over at alpha 1 saturates a neighbouring dab's soft edge and destroys the per-dab hardness curve. CSS/Canvas separable blend modes (lighten, screen) max the colour channels but still use source-over for alpha, so they do not provide a max-alpha operation.
couplings.impact: highest technical risk of the slice; needs a per-pixel coverage mask or a coverage-encoded scratch plus a conversion pass

couplings.title: Per-dab opacity is not representable in the current model
couplings.detail: strokeOpacity derives ONE alpha for the whole stroke from the MEAN pressure, explicitly because Canvas 2D cannot vary alpha within a stroke without per-pixel max blending.
couplings.impact: per-dab opacity must not be promised in the UI; a stamp that varies opacity per dab would break I1

couplings.title: The fill-shape interior is a flat polygon fill, not brush coverage
couplings.detail: rasterizeStroke fills the closed polygon the shape's samples trace with ctx.fill() at the brush colour, then traces the outline. The interior is not covered by dabs. Today this is invisible because hardness and grain are post-passes over the finished coverage.
couplings.impact: under a stamp engine the interior question becomes real; it changes the appearance of every filled rectangle and ellipse

couplings.title: The eraser subtracts the whole buffer live but a bounded region on rebuild
couplings.detail: applyErase calls paintStrokeCoverage with NO region (whole buffer subtracted), while the rebuild path goes through compositeStrokeBuffer with operation 'destination-out' (region-bounded). Equal today by construction; divergent the moment a stamp footprint escapes the region.
couplings.impact: invisible divergence between the live erase and the rebuilt erase

couplings.title: The brush is shallow-copied; a non-primitive stamp field would alias
couplings.detail: createStrokeRecord does brush: { ...brush } and cloneStroke does the same. A shallow spread copies a reference for any non-primitive field, so a stamp descriptor object would be shared between a stroke and its clone.
couplings.impact: latent today (all fields are primitive); a real bug the moment a stamp field is not

couplings.title: A new brush field is silently dropped unless three files change
couplings.detail: The field must be added to BrushSettings, to normalizeBrush (which clamps every field and is always applied by updateBrushSettings), to brushSettingsEqual (which compares every field, otherwise a slider looks dead), and to readBrush (which reads fields explicitly). The serializer needs nothing: brush: element.brush dumps the whole object.
couplings.impact: silent failures in the UI and in the format round-trip

couplings.title: The format version decision is a genuine fork between two written rules
couplings.detail: The project rule says a bump is required when an older reader would render a DIFFERENT PICTURE (SESSION-BRIEF.md section 6). A purely additive, off-by-default stamp field would be ignored by a v8 reader, which would then draw the segment path — the same picture. But SESSION-BRIEF.md section 9 requires v9 and states that an older reader must refuse a v9 file. ROADMAP.md:218-221 is the softer form.
couplings.impact: decides the writer, the reader, the validation rules and the version-rejection test

couplings.title: spacing must stay non-appearance-changing — provable, but fragile
couplings.detail: A dab engine that places dabs by arc length along the polyline of the stored samples is geometrically invariant to spacing, because StrokeBuilder interpolates points on the straight line between raw samples and interpolates pressure linearly. This holds only while interpolation stays linear and the raw point is always appended (addSample drops a raw point closer than MIN_SAMPLE_DISTANCE = 0.05 px).
couplings.impact: if a stamp engine re-interpolates the path or places dabs per sample rather than per arc length, spacing becomes appearance-changing and the format policy changes with it

couplings.title: Brush, eraser and shapes share one rasterizer
couplings.detail: The eraser is a brush whose strokes subtract coverage; the tools differ only in erases. All three reach rasterizeStroke, so a stamp engine changes the eraser and the shape tools as well.
couplings.impact: the slice's blast radius is three tools, not one

couplings.title: The single-dab special case is load-bearing
couplings.detail: extendStroke redraws the whole stroke once it grows past one sample, because the initial dab would otherwise be overdrawn by the first segment's round cap — a second antialiasing pass on the start ring that would make the live buffer differ from undo/reopen/export.
couplings.impact: a dab-based engine changes the shape of this problem; the branch must be re-derived, not assumed

couplings.title: The texture tile cache quantizes a user-visible strength
couplings.detail: textureTile keys the cache by Math.round(clamp(strength,0,1)*20)/20 — 21 buckets — so two strengths inside one bucket share a tile.
couplings.impact: a stamp engine that quantizes a user-visible parameter must document the quantization or the slider appears unresponsive

documentationConflicts.title: Format-version rule vs the slice's acceptance criteria

docA.quote: a bump is required when an older reader would render a different picture, not for convenience

docB.quote: Appearance-changing fields that a v8 reader cannot ignore require format version 9; prove it with tests. [...] Old projects open unchanged; a v9 file requires the new fields and an older reader refuses it rather than drawing the wrong look.

docC.quote: A non-default stamp/dab appearance that an older reader cannot reproduce requires a format bump (v9 if fields change appearance)

documentationConflicts.conflict: A purely additive, off-by-default stamp field would be ignored by a v8 reader, which would then draw the segment path — the same picture the new reader draws by default. By the project rule that needs no bump; the slice's acceptance criteria demand v9 anyway. The readings coincide only if the default output changes or if the v9 field is required and its absence mis-renders.
existingMachinery: src/core/project/projectFormat.ts:696-717 (required-field-per-version precedent for hardness and texture)

documentationConflicts.title: Stale comment inside the pixel test harness
documentationConflicts.quote: Stroke rasterization (paths, arcs) is deliberately a no-op: coverage is seeded straight into the stroke buffer, because these tests are about where that coverage is composited, not about how it was rasterized.
documentationConflicts.contradiction: The implementation rasterizes paths: arc is a 24-gon (1851-1859), fill is point-in-polygon per pixel (1863-1892), stroke is a capsule per segment (1893-1930).
documentationConflicts.impact: a reader who trusts the comment will conclude that no pixel test can check a dab's shape and will defer the proof to a manual browser check; the harness can in fact check spacing, dab count, coverage extent and the union rule (though not an antialiased hardness curve).

existingAudit.headline: Rebuild/undo scales with element count: cost is O(elements x surface pixels); the area half was fixed by R1 (4ac040b), the per-draw cost still needs a profile in the packaged app

rasterBudgetConstraint.limit: 58 bytes per document pixel (3 x 4 x 2^2 + 10), 928 MiB at the cap, inside a 1 GiB budget
rasterBudgetConstraint.implication: a union/max coverage accumulator implemented as a SEPARATE document-sized buffer would be a fourth full-resolution surface = 74 bytes per document pixel = 1.16 GiB, over budget. Precedent: the element-scratch variant F7 was reverted partly for this reason (2fa34cc, audit lines 14-18). Any union mechanism must reuse the existing buffer or be bounded to the stroke's footprint.

gapsNotClosedByThisAnalysis: No browser or packaged-Tauri verification was performed; the brief records both as outstanding for every prior slice.
The React layer has no automated tests, so the toolbar behaviour of a new stamp control can only be checked manually.
The pixel harness has no blur kernel and no 'max' composite, so an antialiased hardness curve and a union accumulator cannot both be proven by the existing harness alone.
No profile was taken in the packaged app, so the dab-count worst case is arithmetic, not a measurement.
